chapter.title: Part III: Moving work forward with Playbooks
chapter.body_html:
Part III covers all 23 Playbooks in pstack.

!

You can skip this part. I recommend reading only the chapters you care about.

You can read the source of each Playbook at any time in the pstack repository. pstack changes often, so it is more reliable to look up the relevant chapter and source file when you need them than to read everything up front.

What Part III shows you

For each Playbook, this part shows you the following.

  • When /poteto-mode picks the Playbook (for example, it picks "Bug fix" for a request that says "repro first")
  • The steps of each Playbook and what each step asks for (for example, "Hillclimb" repeats "one change, one measurement, keep or revert")
  • How a Playbook differs from similar ones (for example, use "Runtime forensics" to find only the cause, and use "Bug fix" to fix it)

A Playbook is a written procedure that turns the steps a skilled engineer takes naturally into a fixed form.

For example, the bug fix Playbook lays out the order: reproduce, find the cause, fix, and verify in the same place. With fixed steps, any agent that takes the work proceeds in the same order.

Playbooks are reference files inside /poteto-mode, and the user does not call them directly. Even so, knowing what is in them tells you which words to put in a request.

!

This book uses only example requests that appear in pstack's sources: the bundled guide, the README, and poteto's guide on X. Four Playbooks have no example request in the sources: Runtime forensics, Trace forensics, Hillclimb, and Pause safely. For these Playbooks, I give no example request. For Hillclimb, I describe only "what to pass in the request" as the bundled guide states it.

The chapters in this part

Chapter Role Playbooks covered
Chapter 10: Investigate and reproduce problems Investigate and return an answer or a diagnosis. Do not change code Investigation, Runtime forensics, Trace forensics
Chapter 11: Fix bugs and improve performance Fix bugs and slowness based on runtime evidence Bug fix, Perf issue, Hillclimb
Chapter 12: Rebuild features, structure, and appearance Add features, change structure while keeping behavior, decide by trying, and match visuals Feature, Refactoring, Prototype, Visual parity
Chapter 13: Write Skills and evaluate them Write Skills that decide how the agent works, and measure their effect Authoring or modifying a skill, Eval
Chapter 14: Open PRs and merge verified changes Open PRs, carry them to merge-ready, and land the verified range in trunk Opening a PR, Babysit, Shipping
Chapter 15: Delegate long-running work to the agent Carry one long piece of work forward without stopping, stop and resume it, and clean up after it Autonomous run, Pause safely, Session pickup, Worktree and simulator cleanup
Chapter 16: Plan many PRs and run them with multiple agents Plan work that spans many PRs, and run it with several agents Multi-phase or multi-PR plan, Orchestrate, Autopilot-full, Autopilot-stack

Chapter 10 through Chapter 12 follow the flow of making one change: investigate, fix, and build. Chapter 13 covers the Playbooks that improve how the agent works. Chapter 14 covers the Playbooks that turn changes into PRs and merge the verified ones. Chapter 15 and Chapter 16 cover the Playbooks that run work over long periods and with several agents.

A quick reference to every Playbook

Playbook Overview When to use it Explained in
Investigation Reads the source code and the change history to answer a question, and returns an explanation or a recommendation with citations When the user asks a question that reading the code or history can answer, such as "how does X work?" or "why was Y built this way?" Chapter 10
Runtime forensics Measures a running process to diagnose the cause of a runtime symptom, and returns the diagnosis without fixing anything When a symptom such as a memory leak or a CPU that spins while idle is still happening, and the agent can measure the running process Chapter 10
Trace forensics Reads a profile or dump handed over after the fact, without rerunning the program, and diagnoses the cause When all you have are artifacts captured in the user's environment, such as a cpuprofile, a trace, a spindump, or a heap snapshot Chapter 10
Bug fix Reproduces a reported bug, finds the root cause, and fixes it with the smallest change that runtime evidence shows is needed When the agent fixes a bug where the result the user gets is itself wrong Chapter 11
Perf issue Captures a trace of measured slowness, compares it with a baseline, and improves performance When the behavior is correct but slow, and the user wants to improve performance with one fix Chapter 11
Hillclimb Improves one metric toward a target by repeating "one change, one measurement, keep or revert" When the user wants to improve one metric repeatedly until it reaches a target, not with a single fix Chapter 11
Feature Decides the shape of the data first, then implements new or changed behavior When the user asks to add a feature or change existing behavior Chapter 12
Refactoring Changes the structure of the code by renaming, extracting, removing duplication, moving, and similar edits, while keeping the current behavior When the user wants to change only the structure of the code without changing behavior Chapter 12
Prototype Builds a throwaway prototype and makes a design decision from what it observes When you want to make a design decision, such as a layout or a behavior, cheaply by building and observing instead of asking a person Chapter 12
Visual parity Treats the baseline's look as the spec and matches the UI pixel by pixel until the image diff is zero When you make two implementations look the same, or migrate the styling system Chapter 12
Authoring or modifying a skill Writes a SKILL.md by a fixed procedure and keeps only the instructions that change decisions during the work When the user or the agent writes a new SKILL.md or fixes one Chapter 13
Eval Measures the effect that a change to a Skill, a structure, or a prompt has on the agent's behavior. It measures blind and before adoption When the user or the agent wants to confirm that a change to a Skill or a prompt works before adopting it Chapter 13
Opening a PR Creates a PR that is ready for review, with small, ordered commits, a Conventional Commits title, and a body in Briefing format When the agent turns changes into a PR at the end of another Playbook's work Chapter 14
Babysit Clears conflicts, review threads, and CI failures, and carries a PR or a stack to merge-ready When the user asks about the state of a PR, such as "get it green" or "keep an eye on PR X" Chapter 14
Shipping Has an agent that did not write the code verify each PR in a stack that passed CI, and merges only the verified range that starts from the root, one PR at a time When the user asks to land a stack that passed CI in trunk Chapter 14
Autonomous run Sets the finish condition first, then carries a long task forward without stopping until the condition is met When the user hands off a long task to completion, as in "loop until it's done" or "use /loop until X" Chapter 15
Pause safely Stops the work at a safe point and leaves a record that an agent that knows nothing can resume from When the user explicitly says to stop, when the user goes offline, when Cursor restarts, or when conversation compaction is near Chapter 15
Session pickup Reads the previous agent's transcript, Cloud Agents URL, or pushed branch, and resumes from where the finished work ends When the user asks to resume or take over work that a previous agent left unfinished Chapter 15
Worktree and simulator cleanup Deletes merged or abandoned git worktrees and old iOS simulators after confirming that they are not in use, to free disk space When the user asks what is using the disk, or asks to clean up worktrees or simulators Chapter 15
Multi-phase or multi-PR plan Writes no code, and produces a checklist-style plan document that settles even how the agent will verify each PR When the agent plans work that spans several phases or stacked PRs before it starts that work Chapter 16
Orchestrate Hands the management of a project that runs for days, with many PRs and subagents, to one coordinator agent that writes no code When the user hands one chat a project that cannot finish within the time one agent can run Chapter 16
Autopilot-full Gives each PR in a queue of independent PRs to its own owner, and merges each one without the operator's review once it passes the coordinator agent's verification When the operator hands off a queue of independent PRs and can give the agent permission to merge Chapter 16
Autopilot-stack Creates and verifies PRs with the same steps as Autopilot-full, but does not merge them. It hands them to the operator as one stack When the operator wants to review before merging, when the changes depend on each other, or when the operator cannot give the agent permission to merge Chapter 16
